The line $y=2x-1$ and the line $y=\frac{3}{4}x+\frac{3}{2}$ intersect at point A. A perpendicular line to the x-axis is drawn from point A, and point B is the foot of the perpendicular. The x-coordinate of point C is $-1$, and point C lies on the line $y=2x-1$. Connect points B and C. What is the degree measure of $\angle CBO$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct $CD\perp x$-axis at D, \\
$\because A(2,3)$, \\
$\therefore B(2,0)$, \\
$\because$ point C has an x-coordinate of $-1$ and lies on the line $y=2x-1$, \\
$\therefore y=2\times(-1)-1=-3$, \\
$\therefore C(-1,-3)$, \\
$\therefore BD=3$, $CD=3$, \\
$\therefore$ triangle $CBD$ is an isosceles right triangle, \\
$\therefore \angle CBO=\boxed{45^\circ}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, point O is the origin. The line $y=2x-1$ and the line $y=\frac{3}{4}x+\frac{3}{2}$ intersect at point A. A perpendicular line to the x-axis is drawn from point A, and point B is the foot of the perpendicular. The x-coordinate of point C is $-1$, and point C lies on the line $y=2x-1$. Connect points B and C. What is the degree measure of $\angle CBO$?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer: Construct $CD\perp x$-axis at D. Since $A(2,3)$, $B=(2,0)$. Since point C has x-coordinate $-1$ and lies on the line $y=2x-1$, $y=2\times(-1)-1=-3$, so $C=(-1,-3)$. Therefore $BD=3$ and $CD=3$, so triangle $CBD$ is an isosceles right triangle. Hence $\angle CBO=45^\circ$.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: The figure has a rectangular coordinate system, O is marked near the origin, A is the intersection point of two slanted lines above the x-axis, B is located on the x-axis and directly below A, indicating that AB is perpendicular to the x-axis; C is located at the lower left and on the steeper straight line y=2x-1. What is required is the angle at point B formed by ray BC and ray BO (leftward along the x-axis).

Reasoning: The two straight lines intersect at A. Solve the equation 2x-1=3/4 x+3/2, obtaining 5/4 x=5/2, so x=2. Substitute into y=2x-1 to get y=3, therefore A=(2,3). Since B is the foot of the perpendicular from A to the x-axis, B=(2,0). The x-coordinate of C is -1, and C is on y=2x-1, so y=2(-1)-1=-3, namely C=(-1,-3). Starting from B, vector BC=(-1-2,-3-0)=(-3,-3), vector BO=(0-2,0-0)=(-2,0). Use the dot product to calculate angle CBO: BC·BO=(-3)(-2)+(-3)(0)=6, |BC|=3√2, |BO|=2, so cos∠CBO=6/(3√2·2)=1/√2. Therefore ∠CBO=45°.
